title: Closed inverse image preserves limits
statement:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a
closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement, and $B$ a sheaf of rings
on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Then:

1. for every weakly contractible affine $V$ in the affine ind-étale basis of
$Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (over an affine open of $X$) and every $B$-module sheaf $F$,
the canonical map $F(v(V))\to(i^*F)(V)$ is an isomorphism, where $v(V)$ is the
henselian lift of [def-exc-closed-site-lift];
2. the functor $i^*$ from $B$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ to
$i^*B$-module sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is exact and preserves all small
limits and all small colimits.

external.place: The weakly contractible affines form a basis of $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 4.2.8), and a morphism of sheaves that is bijective on the objects of a basis is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $L=i^{-1}$ and $R=i_*$ on set sheaves, with unit $\eta$. By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image], $L$ preserves finite limits, has right adjoint $R$, and is computed on underlying sets for abelian sheaves. For an arbitrary ring sheaf $B$, form $LB$ by applying $L$ to its addition, zero, negation, multiplication and one maps. For a left $B$-module $F$ apply $L$ also to its addition and to $\mu_F:B\times F\to F$. The product comparisons give the $LB$-action on $LF$. Each ring or module identity is an equality of composites and products of these maps; applying $L$ proves that identity. This works without commutativity. Naturality makes $L$ of a module morphism linear. This is precisely $i^*F$ as an $i^*B=LB$-module, with no extension along a further ring map. The underlying set sheaf is $L$ of the underlying set sheaf. The description of module sheaves in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] identifies this construction with sectionwise module structures. In particular $i^*$ is additive: applying $L$ to the addition map and to the pair of two morphisms preserves their sum.

proof.text:
Work over an affine open $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$; by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion], its closed inverse image is $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. By [lem-exc-closed-localization], restricting $i^{-1}$ to this square agrees with inverse image of the restricted sheaf. For a weakly contractible $V$ in $\mathcal B_{Z_0}$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-inverse-image-evaluation] to the underlying set sheaves of $F$ and $B$. It identifies the canonical maps into inverse image with bijections
$$F(v(V))\xrightarrow{\sim}(LF)(V),\qquad B(v(V))\xrightarrow{\sim}(LB)(V).$$
These bijections respect products: their composites with either projection are the evaluation maps for the corresponding factor by naturality, so the map for a product is the pair of the two maps. Naturality at addition, zero, negation and $\mu_F$ therefore makes the first bijection additive and linear over the second ring identification. Thus it is the asserted module isomorphism in (1), for the original $F$ as well as its restriction. This uses the evaluation theorem for the particular presheaf $F\circ v$, and does not assert that sheafification leaves every presheaf unchanged on $V$.

source.place: Tag 09BL (lemma-closed-immersion-affines-apply), clauses (1),(2); localization as in Tag 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion)

proof.text:
Still with affine $X_0$, let $(H_a)$ be a diagram of set sheaves indexed by any small category. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] its limit $H$ is computed on sections. On every weakly contractible affine $V$ of $\mathcal B_{Z_0}$ the evaluation theorem gives
$$(LH)(V)=H(v(V))=\lim_aH_a(v(V))=\lim_a(LH_a)(V).$$
Naturality in $H_a$ identifies this bijection with the component of the canonical limit comparison. By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis-wcontractible-cover] every object $T$ of this basis has a cover by such $V$. A sheaf map bijective on these covering objects is bijective on $T$: injectivity follows by separatedness; for surjectivity lift a section on every covering object, check equality of the lifts on the overlaps after covering those overlaps by weakly contractible basis objects, and glue. Basis fibre products and refinements are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], which also says that an isomorphism on the basis is an isomorphism on the full site. Hence $L$ preserves every small limit on this affine square. The argument includes empty diagrams and the empty scheme.

proof.text: For every affine open of $X$, the restricted morphism is a closed immersion of affine schemes, so step 3 applies. [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-inverse-image-limits-zariski-local] therefore gives preservation of all small limits by $L$ on set sheaves globally. Now take a small diagram of $B$-module sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] its limit consists, on each site object, of compatible families of sections with coordinatewise addition and scalar action. Thus forgetting to sets carries it to the set-sheaf limit; the same holds for $LB$-modules. By step 1 the underlying set map of the module limit comparison is exactly the set limit comparison just proved invertible. A bijective linear map has a linear inverse (apply the map to addition and scalar multiplication and use injectivity), and the inverse maps commute with restrictions. Consequently the module comparison is an isomorphism. This proves all small limits in (2).

source.place: Tag 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), proof: limits are Zariski local on X; module limit construction as in the blueprint reduction

proof.text: The inverse/direct-image adjunction lifts to these variable-coefficient module categories as follows. Give $RN$, for an $LB$-module $N$, the $B$-action $R\mu_N\circ(\eta_B\times1)$. The set and abelian adjunctions with the same unit and counit are supplied by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. If $\alpha:LF\to N$ is an abelian sheaf map, its adjunct is $\beta=R\alpha\circ\eta_F$. Apply the set-sheaf adjunction to the scalar-action equations: the action maps are maps of set sheaves, not generally homomorphisms of abelian sheaves. The adjuncts of the two maps $\alpha\circ L\mu_F$ and $\mu_N\circ(1\times\alpha)$ from $L(B\times F)$ to $N$ are respectively $\beta\circ\mu_F$ and $R\mu_N\circ(\eta_B\times\beta)$: for the first use naturality of $\eta$ at $\mu_F$, and for the second use its compatibility with projections, $\eta_{B\times F}=\eta_B\times\eta_F$. Thus injectivity of this set-adjunction bijection says precisely that $\alpha$ is $LB$-linear if and only if $\beta$ is $B$-linear. The $B$-module identities on $RN$ follow from those on $N$ because $R$ preserves products sectionwise and $\eta_B$ is a ring map. Therefore the bijections restrict naturally to module morphisms, giving $i^*\dashv i_*$ for this arbitrary $B$. All products here are binary, and both distributive laws are retained; no commutativity or finiteness of $B$ was used.

proof.text: Every small diagram of module sheaves has a colimit by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the module adjunction of step 5: $i^*$ preserves all of them. In particular it preserves cokernels, while step 4 gives preservation of kernels. In the abelian module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the image of a morphism is the kernel of its cokernel; preservation of both therefore carries each image-kernel equality to the corresponding equality. Together with additivity from step 1 this proves exactness and finishes (2).
